title: A normal ring is integrally closed in its total ring of fractions
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $S$ be the set of nonzerodivisors of $R$ and $Q(R)=S^{-1}R$ its total ring of fractions [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Then every element of $Q(R)$ integral over $R$ lies in the image of the localization map $R\to Q(R)$; equivalently, $R$ is integrally closed in $Q(R)$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 034M (lemma-normal-ring-integrally-closed, line 8218), with its proof

proof.text: Write x = a/s in the total fraction ring, using IsLocalization.exists_mk'_eq [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. For each maximal ideal p, normality gives that A = R_p is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Localization preserves nonzerodivisors (IsLocalization.nonZeroDivisors_le_comap), and these become units in K = FractionRing A. Thus IsLocalization.liftAlgHom constructs an R-algebra map f : Q(R) to K. Integrality maps along f and extends from R to A by IsIntegral.map and IsIntegral.tower_top [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure].

By isIntegrallyClosed_iff K, f(x) is the image of b in A [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Map the fraction identity x times s = a into K. Injectivity of A to K gives a/1 = b times s/1 in A. Hence a/1 belongs to the image of the principal ideal (s), by Ideal.map_span and Ideal.mem_span_singleton [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

Apply Mathlib Ideal.mem_of_localization_maximal to the ideal (s), obtaining a in (s) in R. Ideal.mem_span_singleton yields a = s*r for some r. IsLocalization.eq_mk'_of_mul_eq identifies r/1 with a/s = x [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. This packages the original conductor-ideal argument into Mathlib's local criterion for ideal membership, without a separate invocation of the maximal-ideal existence node.
